title.narrative: The Rakhine State and Union Governments develop and implement progressive policies that reduce violence and promote peaceful coexistence.
The Government implements progressive policies which result in improved trust, reduced violence, and increased adherence to human rights standards.

target.value: Government develop a strategy to address Rakhine State. including on conflict resolution. IDPs. citizenship. movement restrictions. development. and combatting mistrust.

actual.value: The expected long term impact of the program was to contribute to peace and stability in Rakhine state. During the first year of the program up to August 2017, HD supported processes to improve government policy towards addressing the unresolved status of Muslims in Rakhine state. This was done through modelling procedures for expediting citizenship processing for Kaman Muslims, preparations for inter-communal dialogue and contributing to the Rakhine Advisory Commission (RAC)’s reports. Following the events of August 2017 however, HD’s analysis and strategy shifted to addressing the emergent state-driven conflict dynamics. HD effectively established and facilitated new channels of dialogue with harder-to-reach actors affecting the Rakhine conflict, namely the Tatmadaw and ethnic Rakhine politicians. These channels opened new doors of discussion with the Tatmadaw and government about security arrangements for Rakhine state. The channel with political actors achieved informal commitments

title.narrative: Improved policy development and implementation of citizenship issues.
HD's efforts are able to influence the Government's development of policy vis-à-vis conflict resolution as well as to help shape the Government's approach to implementation.

target.value: Notable decline in stateless population in Myanmar; reduction in number of residents of Rakhine reliant on documents without basis in Myanmar law
Muslim trust in government-led citizenship process increases

actual.value: The project assisted the Government’s efforts to address the unresolved status of Muslims in Rakhine State which resulted in 3,000 Kaman receiving citizenship documentation. With the dramatic changes in context, the project reinvested the focus of the small team to engaging the hard to reach actors: the Tatmadaw and Rakhine. Through the later stages of the program, the local partner CDNH became more active in engaging with the Ministry of Immigration on questions of citizenship processing.

title.narrative: Government considers how other policies can foster improved communal relations
CHD's efforts influence the Government's approach to improving communal relations as well as to help shape the Government's implementation efforts.

target.value: Union and State Government further implement rule of law with respect to those that incite and perpetrate violence

actual.value: HD’s advice on implementation was also endorsed by the government and the government-appointed Rakhine Advisory Board. HD seeded the ‘pilot township’ concept through engagement with the Ministry of Social Welfare Relief and Resettlement, the Thailand embassy, the Rakhine Advisory Board who included this in their final report and the UN who have included it in proposals for their future government engagement. This concept was supported by the Minister for Social Welfare who launched a cross-ministerial working group to coordinate its implementation in July 2018, though it is currently stalled for political reasons.

target.value: Increases in freedom of movement enable increased interaction (especially economic) between Buddhists and Muslims

actual.value: Through 2016 and 2017 HD’s analysis was incorporated into the Rakhine Advisory Commission (RAC)’s Interim and Final Report chapters on: Freedom of Movement, Citizenship, Dialogue, Strengthening Trust in the Security Sector, the Relationship with Bangladesh, Regional Relations and the Institutional structures for the Implementation of the recommendations.
